Hi team,

We need a quick compliance pass on the draft listing copy and the proposed support SLA before we submit to AWS and start the co-sell qualification. Attaching two files: redwood_listing_draft_v3.docx and support_sla_matrix.xlsx. High-level asks:

- Branding/claims: Any phrase that could trigger a marketplace policy review (eg "enterprise-grade encryption", "guaranteed latency < 50ms") — flag them.
- Support SLA: The marketplace requires response/ack windows that align with partner program tiers. Confirm whether our proposed Priority/Standard windows map to AWS co-sell expectations.
- Documentation links: We plan to include a link to our SOC 2 summary and an onboarding runbook. Confirm file names/locations.

Timeline: AWS submission target is Nov 12th so we need feedback by EOD Nov 9th.

Quick notes: Jonas — please highlight any operational/infra caveats that would need to be called out (region-specific disclaimers, onboarding lead times). Marissa — please scan for any marketing-y claims that should be tempered. Karthik — check the support matrix against existing Dedicated/Private SLAs.

Thanks,

Thanks Laura — quick pass below. I pulled a few lines that I think will raise flags: 

- "Guaranteed latency < 50ms" — suggest we change to "typical inference latency under 50ms for short-context requests on dedicated instances". Marketplace dislikes absolute guarantees tied to variable infra.
- "Enterprise-grade encryption" — fine if we call out standards (TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest) and link to our security page.
- Any uses of "unlimited" or "real-time" should be avoided. I found one instance of "near real-time" in the feature bullets; I'd keep "low-latency" instead.

Support SLA matrix: the proposed Priority response window (1 hour) is aggressive for hosted tier unless we adjust monitoring/ops runbook. If this is for co-sell joint customers on Dedicated, 1 hour is reasonable if we commit to a follow-the-sun pager. For Hosted we should keep Priority to 2 hours and mark Standard as 8 business hours.

I'll annotate the docx with inline suggestions. Also, we should include the SOC 2 report summary as an inline Drive link (redwood_security_soc2_summary.pdf).

Marissa
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

Adding infra perspective. Key operational notes to call out in listing or in an FAQ:

- Regional availability: Some quantization-backed model builds are only available in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 at GA. Call out the region footprint and note that Dedicated customers can request on-prem or alternate regions with a lead time of 4-6 weeks.
- Onboarding lead times: For Dedicated + co-sell customers, provisioning + validation takes ~10 business days once contract and network peering are in place. For Hosted customers we can usually onboard in 2 business days.
- Metrics: Avoid committing to percentiles across mixed workloads. If we publish latency, use "p50/p95 under typical customer workloads" and include a reference workload description.

I've attached a short ops note into the Drive link (will add to related_links).

Hi Laura — thanks for the heads-up and the drafts. A few quick clarifications from the AWS listing intake team: 

1) Claims: Avoid absolutes ("always", "guaranteed") and benchmark numbers unless you include the test harness. If you want to publish a latency number, include the test conditions (model, batch size, instance type). The excerpt I attached (aws_marketplace_policy_excerpt.pdf) shows the guidance.

2) Support SLA: For an AWS co-sell qualified listing, AWS looks for alignment with partner tiering. Priority (P1) can be 1 hour if you commit to 24/7 support for co-sell customers or to a joint escalation path with an AWS rep. Otherwise the marketplace listing should present the Hosted SLA separately and not promise the co-sell-only response windows publicly.

3) Branding: If you use AWS logos or co-sell badges in marketing assets linked from the listing, you must provide approved artwork and a partner program attestation. Do not embed AWS trademarks in the product description itself.

Next steps: If you can resubmit the listing copy with the edits Marissa suggested and a separate note that clarifies SLA applicability (public hosted vs co-sell Dedicated customers), I can flag it for an expedited intake review.

Jamie O'Neill
AWS Marketplace Partnerships
jamie.oneill@amazon.com
